Hon'ble Sudhir Agarwal,J.
1.
Order dated 12.9.2019 having been recalled vide order of date passed on Restoration/Recall Application, the revision is restored to its original number.
As requested by learned counsels for parties, I proceed to decide this matter finally at this stage.

2. Heard Sri Kapil Kumar, learned counsel for revisionist and learned A.G.A. for State of U.P.
3.
This criminal revision under Section 401 read with Section 397 Cr.P.C. has been filed aggrieved by judgments and orders dated 01.09.1993 and 03.05.1994.

The IVth Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bulandshahar vide order dated 01.09.1993 convicted revisionist and sentenced him to undergo one year rigorous imprisonment under Section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1954") with fine of Rs.2,000/-.

entities.text: IVth Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bulandshahar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Thereagainst, revisionist preferred Criminal Appeal No. 67 of 1993 before Court of Xth Additional Sessions Judge,
Bulandshahar (hereinafter referred to as "Appellate Court") and Appellate Court vide judgment Takur Das vs State And Ors.

entities.text:
Court of Xth Additional Sessions Judge,
Bulandshahar

1 dated 03.05.1994 dismissed appeal confirming judgment of conviction passed by Trial Court.
Being aggrieved, present Revision has been preferred by revisionist.
4. It is contended that there was no compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954.
This aspect was raised by revisionist before Court below also.
Court below found that Public Analyst report was sent by registered post which was received back without service.

Thereafter, it was given to the revisionist in the Court itself after two years i.e. on 28.01.1988 and therefore, valuable right of revisionist under Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 is violated but Court below has said that after receipt of report, revisionist also submitted an application for re-testing, which was rejected by Trial Court and on that basis adverse inference has been drawn against revisionist.
5. It is submitted that compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 is a necessary and mandatory requirement otherwise entire proceedings are vitiated.

6. The view taken by Courts below, I find, is in the teeth of judgment of Supreme Court in Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019) (Arising out of S.L.P. (Criminal) No.
4314 of 2015) decided on 31.07.2019 and in para 15 of judgment, Court has said as under:
"The very purpose of furnishing such report is to enable the Accused to seek for reference to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis if the Accused is dissatisfied with the report.

entities.text: Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such safeguard provided to the Accused Under Section 13(2) of the Act is a valuable right.

In that view even if the despatch of the report on 07.04.1980 is taken as substantial compliance though it is beyond the period of 10 days from 18.03.1980 i.e., the date on which the prosecution was lodged, in the absence of there being proof of delivery of the report to the Accused; in the instant facts the valuable right available to the Accused/Appellant to seek for reference within the period of 10 days stands defeated.
In that circumstance when the Appellant/Accused is made to suffer the penal consequences, it will have to be construed strictly.

In the facts and circumstances of this case, since as already noticed above the report of the Analyst has not in fact been served on the Appellant and the mere despatch of the report as per the statement of PW-2 was not sufficient."
(emphasis added)

7. Therefore, as a proposition of law, it cannot be doubted that prosecution, when challenged, must satisfy that notice issued under Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 has been served upon accused because it is right of accused and prosecution must prove that not only report of Public Analyst was sent by registered post, but it was actually served upon accused-Revisionist, which has not been done in the case in hand.
Trial Court, therefore, has wrongly held that there was compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954.
8. In view thereof, revision is allowed.
Impugned judgments and orders dated 01.09.1993 and 03.05.1994 are hereby set aside.
9. Certify this judgment to the lower Court immediately.
